name: Canyon
notes: Pinyon-juniper and scrub on rocky rims and slopes, cottonwood and willow galleries along the canyon floor stream, ferns at seeps; Colorado Plateau canyons (Grand Canyon, Zion) with Copper Canyon and Fish River Canyon analogues.

canopy.name: Fremont cottonwood
canopy.source: Populus fremontii, SW USA canyon streams, 12-30 m, bright green — USDA PLANTS

canopy.name: Two-needle pinyon
canopy.source: Pinus edulis, Colorado Plateau canyon rims and slopes, 5-12 m — USDA PLANTS

canopy.name: Utah juniper
canopy.source: Juniperus osteosperma, canyon rims and slopes of the Colorado Plateau, 3-8 m — USDA PLANTS

canopy.name: Gambel oak
canopy.source: Quercus gambelii, side canyons and north slopes of the SW USA, clonal deciduous oak 5-15 m — USDA PLANTS

canopy.name: Netleaf hackberry
canopy.source: Celtis reticulata, canyon bottoms and rocky slopes, SW USA and N Mexico, 5-12 m — USDA PLANTS

shrub.name: Coyote willow
shrub.source: Salix exigua, sandbars and stream edges of western N American canyons, narrow-leaved thicket 2-5 m — USDA PLANTS

shrub.name: Cliffrose
shrub.source: Purshia stansburiana, cliffs and rocky slopes of the Colorado Plateau, gnarled shrub 1-4 m, cream flowers — USDA PLANTS

shrub.name: Green Mormon tea
shrub.source: Ephedra viridis, canyon slopes and rims of the SW USA, jointed green shrub 0.5-1.5 m — USDA PLANTS

shrub.name: Big sagebrush
shrub.source: Artemisia tridentata, canyon benches and rims, 0.6-2.5 m — USDA PLANTS

shrub.name: Blackbrush
shrub.source: Coleogyne ramosissima, dark low shrub of canyon terraces and lower slopes, 0.3-1.5 m — USDA PLANTS

shrub.name: Prickly pear
shrub.source: Opuntia engelmannii, lower canyon slopes of the SW USA, 0.5-2 m — USDA PLANTS

ground.name: Indian ricegrass
ground.source: Achnatherum hymenoides, sandy canyon benches, 30-60 cm — USDA PLANTS

ground.name: Galleta grass
ground.source: Pleuraphis jamesii, canyon flats and rims of the Colorado Plateau, 20-50 cm — USDA PLANTS

ground.name: Sand dropseed
ground.source: Sporobolus cryptandrus, sandy canyon floors and washes, 30-100 cm — USDA PLANTS

ground.name: Maidenhair fern
ground.source: Adiantum capillus-veneris, dripping seeps and hanging gardens on canyon walls, 20-50 cm — USDA PLANTS

ground.name: Desert globemallow
ground.source: Sphaeralcea ambigua, rocky canyon slopes of the SW USA, orange-flowered forb 30-100 cm — USDA PLANTS

ground.name: Scarlet monkeyflower
ground.source: Erythranthe cardinalis, streamsides and seeps in SW USA canyons, red-flowered herb 30-80 cm — USDA PLANTS

associations.name: Pinyon-juniper rim woodland
associations.where: rocky canyon rims and mid-slope benches, thin dry soil
associations.source: Brown 1994 Biotic Communities of the Southwestern US, Great Basin conifer woodland; USNVC

associations.name: Blackbrush-Mormon tea slope shrubland
associations.where: hot dry lower slopes and talus, south-facing, shallow soil
associations.source: Brown 1994; USNVC Coleogyne ramosissima shrubland, Grand Canyon Tonto Platform

associations.name: Fremont cottonwood-coyote willow gallery
associations.where: canyon floor stream banks and floodplains with shallow water table
associations.source: Brown 1994 Sonoran riparian deciduous forest; Zion and Grand Canyon riparian

associations.name: Gambel oak-hackberry side-canyon woodland
associations.where: shaded north-facing side canyons and moist upper slopes
associations.source: Brown 1994 Great Basin montane scrub; USNVC Quercus gambelii shrubland

associations.name: Maidenhair fern-monkeyflower hanging garden
associations.where: seeps and dripping alcove walls in the sandstone, constantly wet
associations.source: Welsh 1989 hanging gardens of the Colorado Plateau; Malanson 1980 Zion hanging gardens

associations.name: Sagebrush-ricegrass sandy bench
associations.where: sandy terraces and benches on the canyon floor above flood level
associations.source: Brown 1994 Great Basin desertscrub; USNVC Artemisia tridentata sandy shrubland
